notes:
FICTIONAL DATA, not recovered individuals or a fitted model of the excluded cohort. Exactly 3,000 complete equal-weight rows are generated from a specified external-evidence transport scenario. row_id=1..3000; female=0 male,1 female; age is integer years 20..79; BMI kg/m2; measured SBP/DBP mmHg. All rows represent hypothetical adults already satisfying task eligibility, including no reported pregnancy; unknown/inapplicable pregnancy is not excluded. Actual height/weight, pregnancy status, laboratory weights, HbA1c, diagnosis and treatment are not observed or generated. No medication, hypertension or HbA1c restriction is applied. Eligibility/complete-case selection and peso_lab are not estimable from the permitted evidence; their weighted joint distribution is therefore ASSUMED, not reconstructed. No national representativeness is claimed.

EVIDENCE ACTUALLY RETRIEVED: (1) Moura et al., 2020, Brazilian Journal of Medical and Biological Research, DOI 10.1590/1414-431X20209815, PMC7433850, Table 1 and methods: 15,085 ELSA-Brasil civil servants aged35-74 at 2008-2010 baseline; 54.4% women; male/female BMI27.0(4.3)/27.1(5.1), SBP125.6(16.8)/117.7(16.9), DBP78.9(10.8)/74.0(10.2). These are sex-specific MARGINAL source moments, used only as approximate reference-age location/scale anchors, not falsely as fitted conditional estimates. BP mean of last2 of3 after rest. Occupational urban sample is not the requested population. (2) Linderman et al., 2018 JAMA Network Open, DOI10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2018.1271, PMC6324286, results/methods:1,727,411 Chinese adults35-80, all-treatment sample adjusted BMI slopes1.15 SBP and0.75 DBP per1kg/m2 (5.75 and3.75 per5). Adjustment included demographics, smoking, treatment and other factors, NOT exactly the requested age/sex-only analysis. BP seated repeated electronic readings with conditional third reading. Slopes transported as marginal model coefficients; no claim of causal effects or identical estimates under the requested adjustment. Treated strata had attenuated slopes; treatment mix is an important uncontrolled transport uncertainty. (3) Appeli, Omala & Izudi, 2024 PLOS Global Public Health, DOI10.1371/journal.pgph.0003707, PMC11392332, methods/Table2: 2014 Uganda STEPS analysis n3646, excluded antihypertensive users; residual correlation0.7307 after broader covariate adjustment, BMI categorical, sex not retained by selection. Used only as a rough residual-dependence anchor rounded0.73, NOT an estimate for Brazilian treated/unrestricted adults after the requested adjustment. (4) Barbosa et al., 2020, DOI10.1093/eurheartj/suaa022, PMC7455292: Brazilian MMM2018 opportunistic clinic-heavy volunteers, meanBMI27.3 SD4.5, repeated BP mean readings2and3, obesity/overweight associated with higher adjusted SBP and DBP. Used as contextual corroboration and measurement context, not as representative age, treatment or hypertension prevalence calibration.

ASSUMPTIONS: decade masses .23/.24/.21/.17/.10/.05 and age-dependent female proportions .51/.52/.53/.54/.56/.58 are chosen transport assumptions, not published target estimates. Shifted lognormal BMI with age trend .065/year to55 then-.055/year and sex-specific conditional SD approximated from source marginal SD; extrapolation outside35-74 is unvalidated. BP age trajectories are chosen (SBP quadratic with sex-specific linear slopes; DBP rises gently to55 then falls), and total residual SD14.8/9.9 is chosen to give approximately source-scale BP spread after explanatory variation. Residual dependence0.73 is a rough external anchor. These are fixed scenario parameters, not a posterior or precision warranted by literature. BMI14..60, SBP70..260, DBP40..150, pulsepressure15..140 are broad physiological simulation guards, not claimed release dictionary cutoffs. BMI and paired BP are rejection-sampled rather than clipped; rounding BMI to.01 and BP to.1; guard selection/rounding can change realized slopes/correlation slightly.

MEASUREMENT: BP is baseline final-interview BP, not laboratory-time BP or latent untreated usual BP. For the central scenario, the unknown released final aggregation is treated as approximately equivalent to the repeated seated/last-two mean in external evidence. This is an explicit unverified measurement-transfer assumption, not an assertion about the release. A single final reading or another aggregation could alter variance, residual correlation and associations. Total final-value residuals combine biological variability, omitted risks, medications and measurement error; no extra replicate noise is added, no repeatability is identifiable, and no regression-dilution correction is made.

ANALYSIS: each returned DataFrame has attrs with generated-only OLS estimates from BP~1+age+female+BMI/5, slope SEs, and Pearson correlation of the two residual vectors. Nonlinear generating age effects mean the specified linear-age analysis is an approximation and realized slopes need not equal model coefficients; use flexible-age sensitivity analyses if desired. Realizations are not rescaled to force sample coefficients. Sampling SEs describe fictional-row variation conditional on this scenario, not transport uncertainty. Main sensitivities should vary BMI slopes, residual correlation (e.g.0.60..0.80), age composition, age functions, treatment mix and final-reading precision. The generator uses only numpy/pandas and the submitted seed; observed=None. No files, network, actual measurements or target results are used.
